output_summary:# Verdict: GO

No blocking catalog-policy finding was identified. This GO authorizes only mechanical v24 publication for:

- Git SHA `012e8bec2f8ee3d7bb36a9daa394d2fe1a024b8e`
- Candidate bytes SHA-256 `8f4f5d60707cd57eff560218f3cdeeaf4a56f1934dab9939ba4eeb1630947630`

It does not authorize production migration or deployment.

## Findings

1. Medium, accepted within publication scope — activated runtime privilege expansion.

   The activated policy adds `SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` on all four new tables for `reviewrouter_api`, `reviewrouter_web`, and `reviewrouter_worker`: 48 permissions, of which 36 are new writes. Preactivation retains only 12 reads. This follows the existing blanket runtime ACL at [run-codex-rotating-release-migration.mjs](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/scripts/run-codex-rotating-release-migration.mjs:4773) and its write gate at [line 4851](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/scripts/run-codex-rotating-release-migration.mjs:4851). It is therefore expected, but not least-privilege. The new relations have no RLS.

   Database triggers mitigate the granted mutation surface: envelope revisions reject update/delete; effect and restore ledgers reject delete and constrain updates. Runtime roles cannot disable those triggers because ownership remains with `reviewrouter_release_schema_owner`.

2. Low — the credential history relation broadens access to encrypted credential material.

   `HostedCodexCredentialEnvelopeRevision` stores KMS identifiers, ciphertext, metadata, and hashes—not plaintext tokens. Its constraint rejects `plaintext`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, and `secret` metadata keys at [000075 migration lines 142–188](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/packages/platform/db/prisma/migrations/000075_hosted_codex_security_certification/migration.sql:142). The candidates contain no ARN, bearer token, PEM, URL, or secret-like value. No new provider-instance identity resource appears; `providerResponseIdHash` is hashed effect evidence.

3. Informational — PUBLIC type usage is expected PostgreSQL behavior.

   Seven new PUBLIC `type:usage` grants cover three enums and four automatic table composite types. They do not grant table-data access. The capture gate explicitly permits only PUBLIC schema/type usage at [run-codex-rotating-release-migration.mjs:1819](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/scripts/run-codex-rotating-release-migration.mjs:1819).

4. Informational — no new SECURITY DEFINER routine.

   All seven added public routines are trigger functions using constrained search paths and default SECURITY INVOKER behavior. The new routines and every new relation, index, and type are owned by `reviewrouter_release_schema_owner`; PUBLIC and runtime roles receive no execute grant on them. Existing activation capture/apply routines remain tightly ACL-bound SECURITY DEFINER routines.

5. Informational — promotion remains fail-closed.

   The checked-in promotion code still pins v23 byte count and digests at [promote-private-pg17-activation-catalog-policy.mjs:15](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/scripts/promote-private-pg17-activation-catalog-policy.mjs:15). A no-write attempt to process v24 failed with `activation_catalog_policy_promotion_candidate_size_drift`. Candidate size, whole-file hash, phase digests, normalized shape, and provenance must all be updated before publication; no current bypass was found.

- Activated, 1,384,310 canonical bytes: `sha256:b5b56feebf9be6e17e6d4aaf17d7f5409b7a3df0f6fe5692ea588043d5a7e4c1`

The checked-in v23 artifact and [provenance](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/packages/features/release-rollout/src/domain/activation-catalog-policy-provenance.json:1) also verified exactly: canonical digests match provenance, generated source is exactly canonical, and the referenced v23 review artifact hashes to `324a7dc2763680740a6ba2a2019da4c62b936eac1b3a06a74c3fe4fc42a7b997`.

## Structural delta from v23

| Category | Preactivation | Activated |
|---|---:|---:|
| Roles | 10 → 10 | 10 → 10 |
| Memberships | 5 → 5 | 5 → 5 |
| Reachability | 8 → 8 | 8 → 8 |

There are no removals. The independently constructed expected delta matched exactly: preactivation `100/100`, activated `136/136`, with zero missing or unexpected grants. Effective permissions also recomputed exactly from grants, memberships, and reachability.

Added resources:

- Four tables/RLS entries: `HostedCodexCredentialEnvelopeRevision`, `HostedCodexRestoreItem`, `HostedCodexRestoreOperation`, and `HostedCodexUpstreamEffectAttempt`; all have RLS disabled and no policies.
- Seven types: the four composite row types plus `HostedCodexRestoreItemState`, `HostedCodexRestoreOperationState`, and `HostedCodexUpstreamEffectState`.
- Seven routines: `hosted_codex_effect_attempt_monotonic`, `hosted_codex_envelope_revision_immutable`, `hosted_codex_evidence_no_delete`, `hosted_codex_fence_monotonic`, both restore monotonic functions, and `hosted_codex_terminal_unknown_poison_grant`.
- Seventeen indexes: four credential-revision indexes, four restore-operation indexes, three restore-item indexes, five upstream-effect indexes, and `HostedCodexRelayRequest_id_grantId_key`.

`HostedCodexRelayRequest_id_grantId_key` is the unique composite key created at [000075:304](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/packages/platform/db/prisma/migrations/000075_hosted_codex_security_certification/migration.sql:304) and required by the composite relay-request/grant foreign key at [line 348](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/packages/platform/db/prisma/migrations/000075_hosted_codex_security_certification/migration.sql:348). The candidate correctly excludes the dropped `HostedCodexRestoreOperation_inventory_target_key`, includes its non-unique replacement from [000076:10](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/packages/platform/db/prisma/migrations/000076_hosted_codex_terminalization_restore_invariants/migration.sql:10), and includes the final partial unique index from [000077:10](/var/data/777genius--review-router-saas/worktrees/activation-policy-v24/packages/platform/db/prisma/migrations/000077_hosted_codex_r57_security_race_remediation/migration.sql:10).

## Required publication actions

No candidate or migration remediation is required for policy publication. Mechanically:

- Pin v24 size, whole-file hash, all three canonical digests, audited SHA, readiness reason, and this review’s persisted artifact hash.
- Update the v23 promotion opt-in/constants, reviewed digest trust root, generated artifact, and provenance v3.
- Bind two distinct capture labels to the same exact SHA-256.
- Run no-write promotion verification and require the resulting diff to contain only the intended generated artifact, provenance, and trust-root pins.
- Re-run the normal exact-head checks before merge. Production migration/deployment requires a separate authorization.

## Residual risks

- The external capture paths are mutable; only their exact bytes and hashes are authorized.
- Byte equality proves reproducibility, not independently documented capture lineage.
- The activation policy records ACL/ownership identities, but not index definitions, enum values, routine bodies/SECURITY DEFINER flags, trigger definitions, constraints, or columns. Those were checked against migrations 075–077 at this SHA; any source drift invalidates this GO.
- The blanket runtime ACL and absence of RLS preserve broad cross-table trust among API, web, and worker roles.
- No production access or live deployment validation was performed. The worktree remained clean.
- The repository test runner could not create its cache under the enforced read-only filesystem; no self-reported test result was credited.
